extracted.intended_audience: plain TeX users and macro writers; authors preparing mathematical/technical manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Practical rules, gotchas, and recipes from The TeXbook (Appendix A) for producing correct, well-formatted plain-TeX documents and macros, with emphasis on paragraph/display/mathematical typesetting and page-breaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \leavevmode to begin horizontal mode safely
rubrics_metrics.description: When a macro expands to an \hbox and must work either mid-paragraph or at the beginning of a paragraph, use \leavevmode rather than forcing \indent or requiring users to type \indent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: \leavevmode is an abbreviation for ‘\unhbox\voidbox’. Alternative hack: ‘\ \unskip\hbox{...}’ where a leading \  makes mode horizontal and \unskip removes unwanted space. Avoid inserting unconditional \indent inside macros because that may add unwanted indentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blank spaces rules in modes and tracing
rubrics_metrics.description: Blank space tokens at ends of lines may be digested; only the first typically has effect because blanks are ignored in math formulas and in vertical modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \tracingcommands to inspect what tokens were digested; be aware that blanks inside math or vertical mode are ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mode nesting constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Vertical mode can occur only as the outermost mode; horizontal and display math modes can occur only when immediately enclosed by vertical or internal vertical mode; ordinary math mode cannot be immediately enclosed by vertical/internal vertical mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan macros and environments with knowledge of allowed mode nestings to avoid illegal mode transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid line breaks after en-dash in references
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an explicit protection when you must prevent a break after an en-dash (e.g., ‘exercise \hbox{4.3.2--15}’), though usually ‘exercise 4.3.2--15’ is acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No nonbreaking ~ is needed in typical long ranges; only use \hbox or other protection when a break would be problematic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ~ vs hbox: stretchability and hyphenation
rubrics_metrics.description: The space produced by ~ will stretch or shrink with other spaces in the line; the space inside an \hbox is fixed once set. Using \hbox may prevent hyphenation of words that you might prefer to allow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer ~ when you want flexible interword spacing and allow hyphenation; prefer \hbox only when you need a totally unbreakable unit (but watch for fixed glue and potential unwanted blank at line edges).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unbreakable math/formula techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘\hbox{$x=0$}’ is unbreakable; ‘${x=0}$’ cannot be broken either. A better solution in some cases is ‘$x=\nobreak0$’ to avoid undesired fixed glue and avoid blank space from \hbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of \mathsurround when using \hbox and prefer \nobreak inside math when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent hyphenation or line breaks with penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: \exhyphenpenalty=10000 prohibits breaks at explicit hyphenation points; \hyphenpenalty=10000 prevents breaks after discretionary hyphens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set these penalty parameters when you need to forbid hyphenation in critical contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indentation: \quad vs \indent behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: A \quad inserts an extra em of horizontal skip and, in vertical mode, begins a new paragraph; \indent is implicit at the beginning of every paragraph and doesn’t add double indentation if used twice at the start.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To create double indentation for specific lines, use explicit multiple \indent tokens inside the paragraph body (e.g., ‘\indent\indent’), or use \quad to add extra space where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct discretionary hyphenation for tricky words
rubrics_metrics.description: Define macros with \discretionary to propose preferred hyphenation points and alternative spellings (e.g., \def\ck/{\discretionary{k-}{k}{ck}}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use discretionary hyphens to control hyphenation of irregular words (e.g., 'backen' or 'Bettuch'), but note that TeX won't automatically change spellings like 'eighteen' for hyphenation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define \break as an un-cancellable forced break
rubrics_metrics.description: Define \break as \penalty-10000; \break cannot be cancelled by another penalty and forces a break even if \nobreak is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remember that two penalties in a row behave like a single penalty equal to the minimum of the two original values; multiple \break commands may produce empty lines if consecutive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties combine by taking minimum, and forced break threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: When two penalties appear in a row, their combined effect equals a single penalty whose value is the minimum of the two; breaks are forced when penalty p ≤ −10000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid subtracting large constants into penalties unnecessarily (risk of arithmetic overflow) since values ≤ −10000 already force breaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demerits and visually incompatible lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjacency demerits (\adjdemerits) are added when adjacent lines are visually incompatible (e.g., decent, then very loose, then decent). Plain TeX's default \linepenalty and \adjdemerits are used in line breaking computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware demerits influence line-breaking decisions; consult tracing and adjust \linepenalty/\adjdemerits if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid discarded glue before \par (use \hfilneg before \par)
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX discards a glue item that occurs just before \par; to counteract this when needed, use e.g., ‘\hfilneg\ \par’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert negative glue before \par when you need glue effect to be preserved at paragraph end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \parfillskip to control last-line raggedness
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting \parfillskip=\parindent can help the last line of a paragraph be aligned as desired, but TeX still needs sufficiently long paragraphs or luck to find appropriate line breaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust \parfillskip when aiming for symmetrical paragraph endings; recognize that short paragraphs limit TeX's ability to create ideal breaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy for stubborn raggedness in legacy text
rubrics_metrics.description: As a crude remedy, insert runs of settings such as ‘{\parfillskip=0pt\par\parskip=0pt\noindent}’ at intervals (every ~50 lines) to force paragraph shaping, though this is a hacky approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use restraint — such manual insertions are a last resort and may be necessary when author is 'deceased or set in his or her ways' (humorous admonition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust left/right skips for a paragraph or isolated lines
rubrics_metrics.description: You can set \leftskip and \rightskip for a whole paragraph (e.g., ‘{\leftskip=-1pt \rightskip=1pt htexti \par}’). To change isolated lines, manual intervention per line is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To affect single lines, you must modify line shapes or insert manual glue; paragraph-wide settings are simpler but coarser.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-line macro to create an hbox stretched to \hsize
rubrics_metrics.description: Define \def\line#1{\hbox to\hsize{\hskip\leftskip#1\hskip\rightskip}} to produce an hbox to \hsize that respects left/right skips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displayed equations do not take account of \leftskip and \rightskip; changing those for displays is more difficult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use variable \dimen and box technique for triangular displays
rubrics_metrics.description: A technique using a \dimen register and building a \vbox with a multi-line \parshape can produce triangular-shaped boxed output (example defines boxes and sets \parshape with offsets proportional to \x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiment with \dimen values (examples give numeric values that yield satisfactory heights) and use conditional \ifdim branches to adjust \rightskip/\leftskip and spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \item{} to request hanging indentation at paragraph start
rubrics_metrics.description: Place \item{} at the beginning of each paragraph that wants hanging indentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also possible to use \everypar or other macros for automated paragraph markers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bulleted items: \item{$\bullet$} usage
rubrics_metrics.description: To produce bulleted lists in plain TeX answers, one can use \item{$\bullet$} for the bullet marker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively insert bullets via \everypar or \llap constructs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change \hsize temporarily across paragraphs with automatic restore
rubrics_metrics.description: You can change \hsize for a paragraph and restore it at paragraph end by redefining \par to perform the restore (example provided using \let\endgraf=\par and an \edef restore).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful to reset \par properly to avoid permanent redefinition side effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \parshape for multi-line indented paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: set \dimen0=\hsize \advance\dimen0 by 2em then \parshape=3 0pt\hsize 0pt\hsize -2em\dimen0 to create paragraphs with different line widths and indents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: \parshape allows per-line indentation and width specification for complex paragraph shapes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine short paragraphs into one with \hfil\vadjust{\vskip\parskip}\break\indent
rubrics_metrics.description: To join multiple paragraphs into a single paragraph while preserving visual breaks, use ‘\hfil\vadjust{\vskip\parskip}\break\indent’ instead of \par, and set \hangindent and \hangafter appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long paragraphs consume TeX memory; use restraint. See also \hangcarryover for cross-paragraph hanging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define \hangcarryover to continue hangindent across paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: A sample \hangcarryover macro captures and restores \hangafter and \hangindent across a paragraph boundary using \everypar-like techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when you want consistent hanging indentation across paragraphs without manual resets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting \looseness and \linepenalty trade-offs
rubrics_metrics.description: Using nonzero \looseness forces TeX to work harder; to achieve near-minimal number of lines for a paragraph it is better to set \linepenalty to a small value (e.g., 100) rather than rely on heavy \looseness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: \looseness increases computational effort; prefer tuning \linepenalty for efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of total penalty zero
rubrics_metrics.description: When the total penalty between lines is zero, as between two given lines in an example, no penalty is actually inserted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of zero-value penalty semantics when diagnosing line-break behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sum of interline penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: A relevant penalty between lines is the sum \interlinepenalty plus \clubpenalty plus \widowpenalty (and also \brokenpenalty if the first line ends with a discretionary break).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To control line-breaking near page breaks, set these penalties accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place marginal symbols without opening paragraph height using \strut and \vadjust
rubrics_metrics.description: To insert a marginal star after a line without increasing the paragraph height, use a construction with \strut and \vadjust that assumes the line's depth does not exceed \dp\strutbox; example defines \marginalstar using \vadjust{\kern-\strutdepth\specialstar}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the line depth assumption holds; \specialstar is built as a box of height zero and depth matching \strutdepth so the star doesn't alter paragraph height.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insert bullets automatically with \everypar
rubrics_metrics.description: Define \def\insertbullets{\everypar={\llap{$\bullet$\enspace}}} to add a bullet before every paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous devices can insert hanging indentation or automatic numbering via \everypar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction of displays with preceding glue and paragraph starts
rubrics_metrics.description: When a display begins, preceding \parskip glue and \everypar contents may determine whether there is a partial paragraph before the display; starting a paragraph with ‘$$’ rather than \noindent$$ inserts an indentation that appears on a line by itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of top-of-page glue disappearing and how display starts affect indentation and line shapes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of \penalty50 and its effects on following horizontal list items
rubrics_metrics.description: A break at \penalty50 would cancel \hskip2em\nobreak\hfil, possibly causing the following line to start with text aligned left rather than centered; using an \hbox{} may be more efficient than \vadjust{} in some cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand how penalties interact with glue and \nobreak to predict line layout around displays and signed lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line-breaking algorithm may move hyphens to improve demerits
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX's algorithm might prefer different final-line hyphen placements and could move a hyphen from the second-last to third-last line to reduce demerits; use \tracingparagraphs=1 to diagnose such behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unexpected breaks occur, enable tracing and inspect hyphenation choices; adjust penalties or discretionary hyphens if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer one very bad line to multiple moderately bad lines
rubrics_metrics.description: When distributing extra space, it is often better to have one very bad (underfull) line than several moderately bad ones, since TeX treats very bad lines equally (doesn't distinguish degrees past threshold).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you truly want evenly distributed extra space, adjust \spaceskip to permit more interword stretchability; otherwise accept one bad line for overall better visual appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define \raggedcenter to simulate centered ragged paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Example macro sets \leftskip=0pt plus4em \rightskip=\leftskip \parfillskip=0pt \spaceskip=.3333em ... and sets hyphen penalties high to achieve a ragged-centered effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tuning these parameters controls ragged-center effect; also set \pretolerance/\tolerance to large values to avoid hyphenation and allow line stretching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page-break computations and tolerating badness
rubrics_metrics.description: Page break calculations may produce a tolerable-looking page even with high badness; minor paragraph length changes can shift which paragraph breaks across pages produce better visual results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the page-breaking variables (t, g, b, p, c) and how medskips or shrinkability can allow natural heights to fit; sometimes editing text is the simplest fix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special handling for dangerous-bend paragraphs around insertions
rubrics_metrics.description: When a dangerous-bend symbol is two lines tall, TeX briefly sets \clubpenalty=10000 to prevent breaking between the two internal lines and ensure proper anchoring around insertions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multi-line symbols or blocks, temporarily force penalties to prevent bad breaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: A page must contain at least one box unless insertions are present; beware of box size/depth constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: A page always contains at least one box if there are no insertions; this fails if the topmost box height exceeds 10 pt, or the bottommost box depth exceeds 2.2 pt, or if glue/kern sits between the bottommost box and page break (unless it cancels the depth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure boxes and glue sizes when designing page-breaking behavior to avoid unexpected failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \topinsert and avoid unnecessary \rightline for insertions
rubrics_metrics.description: To place artwork or captions in a top insertion, use \topinsert\vskip...\rightline{\vbox{\hsize ...}}\endinsert, but it's slightly more efficient to avoid \rightline by changing \leftskip (e.g., ‘\leftskip=\hsize \advance\leftskip by-3in’).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid duplicating text reading; preferring leftskip adjustments can be marginally more efficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insertions: \midinsert may be converted to \topinsert if too big for page
rubrics_metrics.description: A \midinsert will jump ahead of other insertions only if it is not carried over; if a midinsert is too big for the intended page it may be converted to a \topinsert and repositioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't assume midinsert placement if insertion sizes exceed available space; compute sizes or use correct insertion class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting/register behavior and examples (\advance, \divide, \multiply)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples illustrate arithmetic idioms in TeX: conditional \advance with negative checks, division/multiplication integer effects, and how stored values change through global/local assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When programming counters and dimensions, be mindful of TeX's integer arithmetic, grouping and global/local effects; consult \tracingrestores for restore behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box handling: \unhbox makes a box void; \unhcopy yields nothing and \setbox effects
rubrics_metrics.description: After an \unhbox\<num>, that box register is void; using \unhcopy yields nothing in some contexts; \global\setbox assignments interact with later \setbox resets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious when reusing box registers; copying versus unboxing has differing side effects.

rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a counter register and \the\count to generate numbering; reset with a clear macro as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insertions may be detached or forced in severe circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Insertions can be forcibly detached if (1) there is no other legal breakpoint so TeX takes an infinite-cost break, (2) \vadjust{\eject} occurs on the same line as a footnote before that footnote, or (3) other \vadjust commands interpose breakpoints before the insertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design insertions and \vadjust uses carefully; unexpected detachments can occur when combined with forced ejects or line-level adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer punctuation outside formulas; spaces near dollar signs vanish
rubrics_metrics.description: Spaces are ignored between dollar signs; punctuation that belongs to the sentence should not be included inside a formula (e.g., end a sentence with ‘$y$.’, not ‘$y.$’).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leave normal punctuation outside math mode; remember that omission of an inter-token space (e.g., no space after 'If') can cause text to run into adjacent symbols inside/outside math.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscript/superscript grouping rules: use braces carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Superscripts and subscripts can be given in either order; braces group multi-token superscripts/subscripts. Do not omit braces around multi-character superscripts (e.g., use '{n+1}^2', not '^2' applied incorrectly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excess braces are harmless; missing braces can cause control-sequence parsing errors or wrong groupings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math punctuation and formula spacing conventions (commas, semicolons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Punctuation in formulas belongs to the textual sentence; putting punctuation into math mode can cause inadequate spacing. For programming-like text, the author disagrees with some style guides that want punctuation to inherit font of preceding character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer to keep sentence punctuation outside math mode to get proper spacing; if you must include punctuation in math, be aware of font and spacing effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing \mathcode (e.g., making '.' act as \cdot) is powerful but dangerous
rubrics_metrics.description: You can redefine \mathcode of a character (e.g., '.' to act like \cdot) but this may be dangerous because periods appear frequently in displayed equations and the change should be confined to limited contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confine \mathcode changes to local groups or specific environments where every period should be a \cdot; otherwise unpredictable side effects occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macros for delimiters and \left/\bigl interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Because \bigl is defined as a macro with one parameter, it requires a delimiter token; \left will fail if the following token is a left brace unless delimiter codes are set appropriately. Best practice: have control sequence names for delimiters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To use \bigl with an explicit delimiter code write \bigl{\delimiter"...}; generally define named macros for commonly used delimiters to avoid surprises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-summation/indexing layouts: use scripts and \atop aligners correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: Use constructs like \sum_{{\scriptstyle ... \atop \scriptstyle ...}} to place multiple indices under/over operators; use \mathop and phantom constructs to adjust limit positions if desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need special positioning of limits or primes, define helper macros (examples: \limsup via \vphantom, custom \sumprime) to obtain consistent placements.

rubrics_metrics.name: When composing matrices and multiline math, use \matrix, \halign, and \eqalign appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples show how to replace explicit hbox-based matrices by \vcenter{\halign{...}} or use \eqalign/\eqalignno for aligned equation blocks; \matrix resets \normalbaselines inside to avoid baseline shifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer higher-level macros (\matrix, \eqalign) when appropriate; define \normalbaselines if you customize baselines for commutative diagrams or other constructs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display-style vs text-style decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Switching to \textstyle (e.g., inside multiline formulas) or forcing \displaystyle inside an \hbox affects glue compression and line-breaking; \hbox freezes glue at its natural width while unboxed displays let TeX compress glue for line fitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \displaystyle for big single-line displays but be aware of differences when putting displays inside \hbox; prefer everydisplay hooks for global formatting changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equation numbering placement affects line height and spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Raising an equation number increases line height and thus inter-line glue; using \smash on raised elements can avoid this added spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust equation numbers carefully; if you raise numbers for aesthetic reasons, consider \smash or other techniques to avoid altering line spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unwanted spaces around binary operators in math
rubrics_metrics.description: When a token like '*' appears in contexts where it isn't binary, TeX may typeset it as Ord and reduce spacing; explicitly bracing tokens or changing \mathcode can control spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want no extra medium spaces for sequences like '(***),' use constructions like '*{*}*' or change \mathcode globally if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \displaylines, \displaymath constructs for multi-line displays with custom left labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples show formatting sequences where left labels are inserted via \llap or \hfill to place equation numbers or labels while keeping display alignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study examples (\displaylines, \eqalignno, \leqalignno) to place labels and numbers consistently; small spacing tweaks (\quad, \qquad) can be needed after viewing the first render.
